title: Mediator and Circuit-Breaker Pattern for Streaming Tool Chains with Provenance Injection
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Multi-tool chains in the execution loop can cause uncontrolled recursion, duplicate calls, and streaming cancellation anomalies. We also lack a consistent provenance tag when injecting tool results into LLM context which makes tracing and fallbacks brittle. This ticket proposes a mediator component that sits between the executor and the tool runners to coordinate streaming-aware circuit-breakers, injection provenance headers, and compatibility adapters for older tool APIs.

Goals:
- Introduce a mediator layer to centralize loop guards (depth, token budget, idempotency) and enforce a per-request circuit-breaker policy.
- Ensure streaming cancellation semantics propagate to all in-flight tool calls and partial streams are checkpointed.
- Attach structured provenance metadata to every injected tool result (tool_id, call_id, hash, schema) to enable deterministic fallbacks and audit logs.
- Provide backward-compatible adapter shims for legacy tool interfaces (old sync HTTP tools, deprecated embeddings endpoints).
- Add e2e tests and perf guardrails to measure overhead (target <3% p50 latency increase) and flakiness reduction.
acceptance_criteria: Mediator component implemented with configurable recursion_depth and token_budget guards
Circuit-breaker triggers for per-tool error-rate and latency threshold and falls back to alternate tool variant
Streaming cancellation propagates to tool runners and partial outputs are checkpointed to KV store
Injected tool results include provenance fields: tool_id, call_id, schema_version, checksum
Compatibility adapters successfully translate at least two legacy tool APIs (sync-http, legacy-embed) with integration tests
Perf regression <=3% p50 for standard gen route in CI perf harness
Documentation (Console + API) and migration guide published
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — prototype mediator event bus implemented in local dev runtime. Observed clean separation between orchestration and tool runners.
2026-03-04: Design review with PM/Design. Decided to use explicit 'provenance' envelope instead of ad-hoc annotations to simplify rollout and RPC compatibility.
2026-03-06: Implemented initial recursion guard (depth=5 default) and idempotency tokens on tool calls. Unit tests added.
2026-03-08: Discovered streaming cancellation edge: partial tool responses kept streaming after parent cancel. Added propagation hook; needs integration test.
2026-03-10: Security review flagged need for KMS-protected call_id rotation for high-privilege customers. Marked as follow-up if customer demands; not blocking initial rollout.
notes: API change is backward-compatible: mediator wraps existing tool runner interface with additional metadata envelope. Plan to ship feature-flagged behind runtime-1.22 and enable for internal fleets before opt-in trial with select customers.
